Vide this award, the Tribunal shall decide the Mact claim petition
bearing no. 150/21, under section 166(4) & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, filed for the petitioners and against the respondents as mentioned in
the memo of parties.
FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

Briefly stated, the facts of the petition are that on 27.01.2021, at about 08:00 pm, one Sarvesh Tiwari (since deceased) was going to his house at Nandgram, Ghaziabad from Dilshad Garden,
Delhi.

It has been alleged that when he reached in front of Pillar No. 254, Sahibabad Railway Station, within the jurisdiction of PS Sahibabad, District Ghaziabad, U.P., one car bearing registration no. DL-2C-BA-6136 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle), came from behind at a very high speed and hit him with a great force.

It has been further alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver i.e. respondent no. 1 (R1) herein, at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without taking necessary precautions at the time of the accident.
Allegedly, above-said Sarvesh Tiwari fell down on the road after being hit by the offending vehicle and he sustained grievous injuries.

The injured was thereon immediately taken to GTB Hospital,
Delhi, where he expired on 14.02.2021.
The postmortem was thereon conducted at mortuary of GTB Hospital, Delhi, vide PM Report no. 144/2021.

An FIR in this regard was also registered vide FIR no. 133/21, for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC, at Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.10.04 16:26:45 +0530 PS Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, UP.
The present claim petition thereafter came to be filed in due course on 20.03.2021.
WS / Reply of Respondents 2.

In the WS filed by respondent no. 1 (R1) ie. the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle, it has been contended that the respondent has been falsely implicated in the present case and that no accident involving the offending vehicle took place as alleged in the claim petition.
The respondent no. 01 denied all the allegations against him and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
3. Herein the present case, the petitioners had initially impleaded the insurance company ie. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Ltd. as respondent in the present case.

in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh. Sarvesh Tiwari ?

10.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.

Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:

However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Manju Tiwari And Ors vs Manoj Kumar Goel And Anr on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101273332/
4 Vehicles Act

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation &
Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand & Ors, 2011 (1) SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

In the present case, the petitioners have examined the eye witness of the accident namely Mohd.
Kasif as their star witness to prove the contentions regarding the claim for compensation, apart from examining the wife of the deceased, as PW2 and PW1 respectively.
Both the said witnesses have categorically stated in their examination on oath that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1 being driver of the offending vehicle.

The said contentions are duly corroborated by the findings of the police as mentioned in the FIR, postmortem report along with other documents pertaining to criminal case in respect of the Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.10.04 16:27:09 +0530 incident in question, brought on record as Ex. PW1/8 (colly) and no ground has been made out by the respondents to disbelieve the same.
12.

The very fact that R-1 has already been specifically arrayed as an accused in case FIR No. 133/21,
PS Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, UP, for the offences u/s 279/ 338 IPC is itself a strong circumstance to support the above said testimony of PW-1 and PW-2 on these issues.

The copies of FIR, Site plan,
report u/s 173 Cr.PC, mechanical inspection report and postmortem report, brought on record as Ex. PW1/8 also corroborate the oral testimony of PW-1 & PW2.

Moreover, the position of law in this regard has been made clear in the case of "National Insurance Co., Vs Puspha Rana", 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, wherein it has been held that filing of Chargesheet is sufficient proof of the negligence and involvement of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Vs Puspha Rana", 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi

sentences.text:
Similar observations have been made in the case of "United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors.", 2014 (2) Tac 846 Del, that if the claimant was able to prove the criminal case on record pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle,
whereby the criminal records showing completion of investigation by the police and filing of Chargesheet under Section 279/304-A/337 IPC against the driver have been proved, then, the documents mentioned above are sufficient to establish the fact that the driver was negligent in causing the accident.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors.", 2014 (2) Tac 846 Del
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where FIR is lodged, Chargesheet is filed, especially in a case where driver after causing the accident had fled away from the spot, then the documents mentioned above are sufficient to establish the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident particularly when there was no defence available from his side before the Learned Tribunal.

The position of law has been recently reiterated by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:

Anr. " arising out of SLP (C ) No. 10351/2019, wherein it has been held that:-

Even if the eye witnesses are not examined, that will not be fatal to prove the death of the deceased due to negligence of the bus driver."

13. Besides the above, respondent no. 1 namely Manoj Kumar was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW-2 regarding the above accident and its manner etc., but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi).
14.

sentences.text: Furthermore, respondent no. 1 i.e. driver-cum-owner and respondent no. 2 i.e. Insurance Company, have neither impeached the testimony of PW-1 & PW-2 nor they have led any defence evidence to substantiate their claim that the accident was caused due to fault of the deceased or that they have been falsely implicated in the present case.

The evidence of the star witness in this case i.e.
PW-2, on the aspect of rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle,
has remained unimpeached and his testimony has to be accepted on its face value itself as the same has successfully stood the test of cross-examination.

Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.10.04 16:27:20 +0530 15.

In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the offending vehicle was being driven by R-1 indeed at the time of incident and the fatal injuries to the deceased took place on account of the incident in question itself.

16. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle) hit the deceased Sarvesh Tiwari from the back side.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the fatal injuries to the deceased Sarvesh Tiwari.

17. Furthermore, in view of the medical records, postmortem report placed on record by the petitioners, no doubt or dispute is left regarding the fatal injuries to the deceased Sarvesh Tiwari in the above accident.

The issue at hand is thus decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioners.
Issue no. (ii) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP. 
19.

On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by R-1 and fatal injuries had been caused to the deceased in the incident.

Hence, the petitioners being LRs are entitled to compensation in this case as the claim of the petitioners being dependent of the deceased has neither been denied nor disputed in any manner by the respondents during the entire proceedings.
20. The issue at hand is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.
LIABILITY 21.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
The respondent no. 1 Manoj Kumar is the principal tort feasor being driver and also vicariously liable being the owner of the offending vehicle.

Herein, it is pertinent to note that the respondent no. 2 i.e. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company has specifically admitted in its written statement that the offending vehicle was duly insured at the time of accident vide policy no.
3001/MI-792718/00/000 for third party liability, in the name of Sh. Manoj Kumar Goel i.e.
respondent no. 1 (R1) herein, with its validity from 02.09.2019 to 01.09.2022.

At the same time, the respondent no. 2/insurance company has failed to bring on record Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.10.04 16:27:32 +0530 or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the respondent no. 1 in any manner.
22.

Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent no.2 i.e. insurance company, is liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioners on behalf of respondent no. 1 without any recovery rights.

As far as computation of compensation is concerned, the same shall be under the following heads :-

It is clear from above stated facts and circumstances that the deceased had expired on 14.02.2021 ie. 17 days after the accident and no medical expenditure was undertaken by the petitioners in the treatment of the deceased at the govt. hospital before his death.
Hence, petitioners are not entitled to any compensation under this head on account of absence of any evidence brought on record in this regard.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 25.

In the present case, perusal of the Aadhar card of the deceased Ex. PW1/7, reveals that date of birth of the deceased was 01.01.1966 and the same has not been disputed in any manner by the respondents.
Therefore, the deceased was thus aged 55 years 1 months 13 days at the time of the incident resulting in his death on 14.02.2021.

Petitioner Smt. Manju Tiwari (PW1) in her deposition has stated that at the time of accident, her deceased husband was working in Himachal Maharashtra Transport Company at Delhi and that he was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month.

However, the petitioners have failed to bring any evidence on record pertaining to the employment in any establishment at Delhi or in respect of the alleged monthly income of the deceased Sarvesh Tiwari to show that he used to earn Rs. 20,000/- per month or that he possessed any specific skill.
Nevertheless, the petitioners have brought on record the 10th Marksheet of the deceased as Ex. PW1/9.

It is pertinent to note that the accident in question took place at Sahibabad, UP and the family members of the deceased ie. petitioners and the victim were residents of the State of U.P. at the time of the accident.
Therefore, this Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased at parity with ' Semi-skilled worker ' of U.P. prevalent at the time of accident i.e. Rs. 9,634/- per month on the date of accident.

27. Furthermore, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court titled as "National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680", 10% addition shall be given to the deceased towards future prospects as he was below 60 years at the time of incident and he was self employed.

LOSS OF CONSORTIUM / LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION 30.

In "Magma Vs. General Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Nanu Ram & Ors". 2018 ACJ 2782, it was observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court that 'consortium' is a compendious term, which encompasses 'spousal Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.10.04 16:27:51 +0530 consortium', 'parental consortium' and 'filial consortium'.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance,
solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his entire family.

entities.text: Magma Vs. General Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Nanu Ram & Ors". 2018 ACJ 2782

sentences.text:
Spousal Consortium allows compensation to surviving spouse for loss of 'company, society,
co-operation, affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation'.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court further observed in said judgment that parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of 'parental aid,
protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training.
Similarly, filial consortium is to be granted to each of the surviving dependent parents on the death of their child.

31. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, the computation of compensation under this head is as follows :
Filial Consortium : Rs. 48,000/- (Rs. 48,000/- X 1) Spousal Consortium :

Parental Consortium : Rs. 1,92,000/- (Rs. 48,000/- X 4)
32.
Hence, the petitioners are hereby awarded a total sum of Rs. 2,88,000/- on account of loss of consortium/loss of love and affection under this head.

opennyai_summary.issue:
From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 27.02.2024, as under:-
(i) Whether respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle no. DL2CBA6136 on 27.01.2021 at about 12 midnight in front of pillar no.
254, Sahibabad Railway Station, Ghaziabad, UP, within the jurisdiction of PS Sahibabad, Ghaziabad,
in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh. Sarvesh Tiwari ?
OPP. 
(ii) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
Issue no. (ii) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
LIABILITY 21.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Manju Tiwari And Ors vs Manoj Kumar Goel And Anr on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101273332/
4 Vehicles Act
, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation &
Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand & Ors, 2011 (1) SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.
Both the said witnesses have categorically stated in their examination on oath that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1 being driver of the offending vehicle.
Where FIR is lodged, Chargesheet is filed, especially in a case where driver after causing the accident had fled away from the spot, then the documents mentioned above are sufficient to establish the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident particularly when there was no defence available from his side before the Learned Tribunal.
"It is settled in law that once a charge-sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi).
14.
Furthermore, respondent no. 1 i.e. driver-cum-owner and respondent no. 2 i.e. Insurance Company, have neither impeached the testimony of PW-1 & PW-2 nor they have led any defence evidence to substantiate their claim that the accident was caused due to fault of the deceased or that they have been falsely implicated in the present case.
The evidence of the star witness in this case i.e.
PW-2, on the aspect of rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle,
has remained unimpeached and his testimony has to be accepted on its face value itself as the same has successfully stood the test of cross-examination.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the offending vehicle was being driven by R-1 indeed at the time of incident and the fatal injuries to the deceased took place on account of the incident in question itself.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle) hit the deceased Sarvesh Tiwari from the back side.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the fatal injuries to the deceased Sarvesh Tiwari.
On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by R-1 and fatal injuries had been caused to the deceased in the incident.
Hence, the petitioners being LRs are entitled to compensation in this case as the claim of the petitioners being dependent of the deceased has neither been denied nor disputed in any manner by the respondents during the entire proceedings.
Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent no.2 i.e. insurance company, is liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioners on behalf of respondent no. 1 without any recovery rights.
It is clear from above stated facts and circumstances that the deceased had expired on 14.02.2021 ie. 17 days after the accident and no medical expenditure was undertaken by the petitioners in the treatment of the deceased at the govt. hospital before his death.
Hence, petitioners are not entitled to any compensation under this head on account of absence of any evidence brought on record in this regard.
In the present case, perusal of the Aadhar card of the deceased Ex. PW1/7, reveals that date of birth of the deceased was 01.01.1966 and the same has not been disputed in any manner by the respondents.
Therefore, the deceased was thus aged 55 years 1 months 13 days at the time of the incident resulting in his death on 14.02.2021.
Therefore, this Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased at parity with ' Semi-skilled worker ' of U.P. prevalent at the time of accident i.e. Rs. 9,634/- per month on the date of accident.
Moreover, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of "Sarla Verma &
Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr"., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitutional Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of " National Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs Pranay Sethi & Ors".
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the total loss of dependency qua the deceased in the present case comes out to be Rs. 95,376/- X 11= Rs. 10,49,136/-.
